verdict.rationale: Grok Build documents running multiple agents in parallel. Worktree sessions isolate parallel agents so they cannot overwrite each other's files, subagents run as independent child sessions that can work in the background, and a dashboard tracks every session's status. The 'for hours or days' autonomy part of the story is not evidenced. Missing for 10: evidence of long-running (hours/days) unattended execution, a documented way to launch a fleet of agents at scale (e.g. cloud/remote agents), independent or hands-on corroboration of parallel fleet usage.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can launch fleets of autonomous agents that work in parallel on different tasks for hours or days

citations.quote: A worktree session runs in an isolated copy of your repository, so parallel agents cannot overwrite each other's files.
Subagents are independent child sessions with their own context.
Grok can run commands, subagents, and monitors in the background while the conversation continues.
The dashboard is a fullscreen overview of every session: which agents need input, which are working, and which are done.
